I think it makes sense to have `use_blend`, but I believe we need two PRs to accomplish this. Therefore, I suggest that we should first create a PR that extends the `Animation` class to create `PolyphonicAnimation`, as in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/71855.

This will allow `AnimationTrack` to safely override `AnimationPlayer` in the same way that `AudioTrack` overrides `AudioStream` with `AudioStreamPolyphonic` (solve https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/8783). Also it should allow you to reduce the large number of lines you currently have in the `case TYPE_ANIMATION` case statement in this PR to the equivalent of `case TYPE_AUDIO`. As a byproduct, it should also allow you to queue identical animations (partially solve https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/72484).

Then, we would implement something similar to `AudioTrack` in the `AnimationMixer`, but I believe that the two processes should be largely unified. In other words, `PlayingAudioStreamInfo` and `PlayingAnimationInfo` should be based on a single struct like `PlayingSequenceInfo`. Although I suppose we could extend `PlayingSequenceInfo` to handle that if necessary (e.g. if `AudioTrack` has volumes for individual keys), but I don't think that's in the scope of your PR.

### **Short summary to the AnimationTrackPlugins class**
I completely re-wrote the class.

There is now an inner class called **AnimationTrackEditKey**. 
It adopts the logic of a key on the timeline and you can implement new key types more quickly by overwriting them:

```
Ref<Resource> get_resource(...) // resource of the key (AudioStream, Animation, ...)
float get_start_offset(...) // start offset of the key
float get_end_offset(...) // end offset of the key
float get_length(...) // total length of the key
void set_start_offset(...) //sets the start offset of the key
void set_end_offset(...) {} //sets the end offset of the key
StringName get_edit_name(...); //name of the key
```

Default is a simple empty key without a length and without a resource behind it.

You can also override:
```
void get_key_region_data // data to visualize the key if the key has a length
```

so that you can visualize the key if the key has a length (which would be the case with **AudioStream** and **Animation**)

For _get_key_region_data_ on **AudioStream**, he uses the **AudioStreamPreview**-class to create the necessary data.
For _get_key_region_data_ on **Animation**, he uses the **AnimationPreview**-class to create the necessary data.

_NOTICE_: The class has some constant definitions that change the appearance of a key:
```
#define REGION_RESIZE_THRESHOLD 5.0
#define REGION_MAX_WIDTH 4.0
#define REGION_FONT_MARGIN 3.0
#define REGION_DEFAULT_FONT_SCALE 1.5
#define REGION_BG_COLOR Color(0.25, 0.25, 0.25)
#define REGION_EDGE_ALPHA 0.7

#define COLOR_EDIT_SAMPLE_INTERVAL 64
```

Maybe these can be better controlled using themes (get_theme_..) or somehow different. But these were also previously static in the code. Just not layed out.

### **Short summary to the AnimationMixer class**
I changed the logic of **Type Animation**.
It is now more accurate when it comes to play or seek.

Also the animation shows visually correctly now if you go before the first key on the timeline. Especially when it comes to timeline jumps using "seek".
Before there was an undefined behavior. Depends on which animation was currently active.

The same applies to the **[stop]**-keys.
A **[stop]**-key is no longer in the behaviour where the last animation and its frame are retained.
**[stop]**-key now works as if it were actually stopping the animation. So a **[stop]**-key can now be used logically. 

### **What's Next?**
- **use_blend** is not yet implemented.
- And overlapping animation logic exists to some extent, but no **interpolation between animations** occurs yet.
- If an animation on the timeline has a loop, **it continues to loop even after the length of the key**, in play-mode. Needs to be fixed maybe on the play(...) function of the AnimationPlayer.
- changed **start offset and move selection position popping** issue. Also issue when start offset goes over previous key.
- key **selection and hover issue** because of wrong hit rect calculation.
- Furthermore, there are a **few visual issues regarding the timeline and tracks** and its width. It is just visual, but I should also go through that. But it must have been there before. There is an inconsistency somewhere.

First of all, this PR failed to rebase and has reverted a lot of previous changes in the master, so it needs to be rebased correctly.

Second, this PR changes too much at once.

As I mentioned earlier, the current Animation base lacks the implementation to handle AnimationTrack with safe way, so implementing something like PolyphonicAnimation is necessary first.

Implementing that PolyphonicAnimation is synonymous with verifying whether AnimationTracks can be correctly blended from AnimationMixers without GUI, and it will also be where we achieve commonality with AudioTracks; This sequence allows you to significantly reduce the code duplication with AudioTracks present in this PR. Doing it the opposite way can cause unexpected compatibility breaks, which we need to avoid. There is a sequence for implementing a large object safely, just as we clear the ground before building a cabin.
